tls_echo_client Example

TLS client with certificate checking. Usage: tls_echo_client host port [--ca ca.pem] [--insecure]

Contents

Building and Running
Source

Building and Running

examples/tls/tls_echo_client.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as tls_echo_client (cmake-build/examples/tls_echo_client on Linux, cmake-build\examples\Release\tls_echo_client.exe on Windows) and run by tests/run_tests.sh. See Building and Running for the build commands. The comment at the top of the file describes the program. Back to the example programs.

TLS echo client. Connects to tls_echo_server, sends each line read
from standard input and prints the reply. The server certificate is
checked against the system certificate store, or the CA file given
with --ca. --insecure skips the check (test servers only).

Usage: tls_echo_client host port [--ca ca.pem] [--insecure]
*/
// ----------------------------------------------------------- // 
#include "gxdlcode.h"

#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <iostream>
#include "gxstls.h"

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  if(argc < 3) {
    std::cerr << "Usage: " << argv[0] 
              << " host port [--ca ca.pem] [--insecure]\n";
    return 1;
  }
  gxsTLSConnection conn;
  for(int i = 3; i < argc; i++) {
    if(strcmp(argv[i], "--ca") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) conn.SetCAFile(argv[++i]);
    else if(strcmp(argv[i], "--insecure") == 0) conn.SetVerifyPeer(false);
  }
  conn.SetTimeout(30);
  if(conn.Connect(argv[1], std::atoi(argv[2])) != 0) {
    std::cerr << conn.Error() << "\n";
    return 1;
  }
  std::cerr << "Connected with TLS to " << argv[1] << "\n";

  std::string line, reply;
  while(std::getline(std::cin, line)) {
    if(conn.SendLine(line) < 0) {
      std::cerr << conn.Error() << "\n";
      return 1;
    }
    if(line == "quit") break;
    if(!conn.ReadLine(reply)) {
      std::cerr << "Connection closed" << "\n";
      break;
    }
    std::cout << reply << "\n";
    if(line == "shutdown") break;
  }
  conn.Close();
  return 0;
}
